subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for September 01, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Outcomes of patients with Waldenström macroglobulinemia in ICU
sentences: Story 1 is about Outcomes of patients with Waldenström macroglobulinemia in ICU: a retrospective multicentric study..
This is a recent research article from Journal of critical care.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in ICUs including all patients with WM admitted between 2010 and 2024, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
A total of 151 patients with WM were admitted to the ICU over the 14-year period.
ICU mortality was 20% (n = 30), with infections being the leading cause of death.
The most WM-specific complications included hyperviscosity syndrome (n = 29, 19%) and other IgM-related vascular complications (n = 27, 18%).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.

script.heading: Story 2 - Probiotic Implementation and Necrotizing Enterocolitis Risk in
sentences: Story 2 is about Probiotic Implementation and Necrotizing Enterocolitis Risk in Preterm Infants..
This is a recent research article from JAMA network open.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in ICUs in the Netherlands, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
This study included 1413 infants (742 males [52.5%]), stratified into a preimplementation group (n = 598) and a postimplementation group (n = 815).
Following probiotic implementation, NEC incidence decreased from 11.9% (n = 71) to 5.3% (n = 43) (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.49 [95% CI, 0.34-0.70]; P < .001).

All-cause mortality remained stable for the preimplementation and postimplementation groups (70 [11.7%] vs 94 [11.5%]; ARR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.82-1.39]; P = .64); non-NEC-associated mortality increased from 7.2% (n = 43) to 9.6% (n = 78) (ARR, 1.42 [95% CI, 1.01-1.98]; P = .04).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Story 3 - Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare
sentences: Story 3 is about Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes..
This is a recent research article from JAMA internal medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in Critically ill or ICU-relevant patients described in the abstract; confirm eligibility criteria in the full text., how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%).

Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days).

VE against RSV-associated death was 56% (95% CI, 39%-69%), VE against severe RSV-associated outcomes was 59% (95% CI, 44%-70%), and VE against RSV-associated thromboembolic events was 66% (95% CI, 44%-79%).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Outcomes of patients with Waldenström macroglobulinemia in ICU: a retrospective multicentric study.

The most WM-specific complications included hyperviscosity syndrome (n = 29, 19%) and other IgM-related vascular complications (n = 27, 18%). The one-year mortality rate was 40% (n = 58) and remission at one year was achieved in 47% (n = 56) of treated patients. articles.title: Probiotic Implementation and Necrotizing Enterocolitis Risk in Preterm Infants.
articles.summary: Preterm infants (<30 weeks of gestational age [GA], birth weight [BW] <1000 g, or both) born between January 1, 2018, and July 1, 2024, were compared before and after the implementation of routine probiotic supplementation. The probiotic protocol was introduced in October 2020 or March 2021, depending on the center. The primary outcome was NEC incidence, classified as medical, surgical, or fatal. This study included 1413 infants (742 males [52.5%]), stratified into a preimplementation group (n = 598) and a postimplementation group (n = 815). Following probiotic implementation, NEC incidence decreased from 11.9% (n = 71) to 5.3% (n = 43) (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.49 [95% CI, 0.34-0.70]; P < .001).

articles.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes.
articles.summary: To be eligible for inclusion in a cohort, a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary must be aged 65 years or older, reside in a US nursing home during the study period for at least 1 day, have continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A and B (365 days prior to the index date), and have continuous enrollment in Part D (beginning on June 21, 2023). Outcomes were RSV-associated hospitalization, RSV-associated death, severe RSV-associated outcomes (intensive care unit or critical care unit admission, medical ventilator use, or RSV-associated death), and RSV-associated thromboembolic event. VE was calculated as (1-HR) × 100%. Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days).
